report.text:
## Outcome

The team established **the entire stated formula**, not merely the cubic and four-regular cases. Extremizers can be chosen cubic when \(n\) is even and four-regular when \(n\) is odd. They ultimately proved that every other possible degree gives no larger commute time.

No finding contradicts the supplied answer. Several intermediate conjectures and attempted arguments failed, but none is used in the final proof.

## Proof framework

Give every edge unit resistance and write \(R_G(u,v)\) for effective resistance. The electrical commute identity gives, in a \(d\)-regular graph,
\[
\mathbb E_uT_v+\mathbb E_vT_u=dn\,R_G(u,v).
\]
Thus the problem becomes maximizing \(d\) times the resistance diameter, followed by multiplication by \(n\).

The proof combines series decomposition at bridges and articulation vertices, capacitated-flow energy bounds, Foster’s identity, and exhaustive **exact rational** enumeration of small exceptional graphs.

## Even orders: sharp cubic bound and constructions

For cubic graphs they proved
\[
R_{\max}\le
\begin{cases}
n/2-9/4,&n\equiv2\pmod4,\\
n/2-11/4,&n\equiv0\pmod4.
\end{cases}
\]

Delete bridges and follow the bridge-block path between the marked vertices, assigning off-path branches to their attachment blocks. Every nontrivial bridgeless cubic block is two-vertex-connected, so two internally disjoint paths give resistance at most one quarter its order. Every component beyond a bridge contains at least five vertices.

A defect accounting makes the bound sharp: each terminal block contributes at least \(5/8\), internal blocks contribute nonnegative defect, and a nonstandard block adds at least \(1/2\). All-standard chains have order \(10\bmod4\), forcing that extra defect for \(n\equiv0\bmod4\).

The necessary small terminal resistance maxima are \(7/8\) on five vertices and \(11/8\) on seven vertices. These were exhaustively checked.

Equality constructions join two five-vertex caps, or one five- and one seven-vertex cap, by bridges and copies of \(K_4-e\). Each diamond adds four vertices and resistance two including its associated bridge increment. Multiplication by \(3n\) yields exactly the two even formulas.

Authoritative files: `even_cubic_proof.md`, `check_even_terminals.py`, and `even_terminal_check.json`.

## Four-regular graphs: the odd residue constants

The central all-order local lemmas concern two-connected graphs whose ports have degree two and all other vertices degree four:
\[
R_{\text{two-port}}\le(3b+2)/16,\qquad
R_{\text{cap}}\le3b/16-13/40.
\]

Their proof uses maximal nested chains of two-edge cuts. Prescribing current \(1/2\) on interface edges, maximality and even-cut parity permit internal currents bounded by \(1/4\). Energy charging handles arbitrary size; only small layers and endpoint tails require exact checks.

For orders \(6,\ldots,13\), exhaustive two-connected cap/two-port maxima were:
\[
\begin{array}{c|rrrrrrrr}
b&6&7&8&9&10&11&12&13\\ \hline
\mathrm{cap}&4/5&104/115&36/35&52/45&31/20&91/55&9/5&343/180\\
\mathrm{two\ ports}&5/4&4/3&3/2&19/12&2&25/12&9/4&7/3
\end{array}
\]
The degree-sequence generator uses justified symmetry pruning, not random sampling; the final enumeration covered 639,086 generated representatives through order thirteen.

Articulation-path decomposition and exact min-plus optimization modulo five then give
\[
R_{\max}=n/4-C_r,\qquad
(C_0,C_1,C_2,C_3,C_4)
=\left(\frac75,\frac{23}{20},\frac{149}{115},\frac75,\frac{139}{90}\right)
\]
for allowed odd orders. Off-path branches carry enough vertices to make branching uncompetitive. Pairs not separated by an articulation satisfy a stronger bound.

Equality uses caps of orders \(6,7,9,10\), with root eccentricities
\[
4/5,\quad104/115,\quad52/45,\quad31/20.
\]
The standard middle module has order six, resistance \(5/4\), and a \(K_4\) core; an exceptional order-eight middle module has resistance \(3/2\). Identify degree-two ports to concatenate modules. Base chains by \(n\bmod5\) are:
\[
(6,10),\quad(6,6),\quad(6,7),\quad(6,\text{middle }8,6),\quad(6,9).
\]
Additional standard middle modules add five vertices and resistance \(5/4\). Multiplying by \(4n\) gives all four odd branches of the supplied formula.

Main files: `odd4_upper_agent1.md`, `maximal_2cut_chain_agent4.md`, `odd_lower_proof.md`, `odd_construction.py`, `enumerate_local4.py`, `enumerate_local4_sage.py`, and the `local4_exact*.json` tables.

## Why other degrees cannot win

This was the last substantial gap, and it was eventually closed.

* Degree two gives \(dR_{\max}\le n/2\).
* For \(d\ge n/2\), complement-Laplacian bounds give
  \[
  R(u,v)\le2/(2d-n+2),\qquad dR(u,v)\le n/2.
  \]
* Four-regular graphs of even order are below the cubic target.
* At even orders, degrees five and six satisfy
  \[
  dR_{\max}\le3n/2-33/4.
  \]
  The proofs use constant-width cut chains, acyclic integral-flow length bounds, bridge reassembly, and exact small-tail certificates.
* At even orders, every \(d\ge7\) satisfies
  \[
  dR_{\max}\le
  \frac{d^2+8d+3}{(d+1)(d+2)}n-d-2+\frac2{d+2},
  \]
  below the cubic target. This combines Foster’s identity with improved adjacent-edge resistance bounds for vertices that are not closed-neighborhood twins.
* At odd orders, parity forces even degree. Degrees six and eight satisfy
  \[
  dR_{\max}\le n-278/45.
  \]
  A carefully constructed two-level hierarchy of two- and four-edge cuts makes interface currents consistent; singleton-layer charging and small dense-atom checks finish the bounds.
* For odd orders and \(d\ge10\), a shortest-cycle chord-counting argument combined with Foster’s identity gives
  \[
  dR_{\max}\le
  \frac{d^2+15d-8}{2(d+1)^2}n
  -\frac{d^3+4d^2+15d-8}{2(d+1)^2},
  \]
  strictly below every odd target.

Corresponding writeups include `even_degree5_agent1.md`, `even_degree6_agent3.md`, `even_degree7plus_agent3.md`, `odd_degree6_agent4.md`, `odd_degree8_core_agent2.md`, `d8_endpoints_agent4.md`, and `odd_degree10plus_agent1.md`.

## Failed approaches and final certificate

They did **not** prove the proposed broad minimum-degree resistance inequalities; these remain unnecessary conjectures. A changing-width “arrival-capacity” flow construction was explicitly disproved by a small quotient-network counterexample and discarded. A proposed uniform defect gap was also refuted by a seven-vertex two-port example.

The final artifact is `workspace/regular_graph_proof_certificate.zip` (46 files), with integrated proof at `workspace/complete_certificate_agent1/PROOF.md`. Its `RUN_ALL.py` recomputed every proof-critical finite table and rational check, plus cubic constructions through order 40 and odd constructions through order 65. The bundled run passed in 43.99 seconds; `verification.log` and a SHA256 manifest are included. No mathematical case remained unresolved.
